proposals.whatItIs:
ARC is a ChargeItSpot product. The MHI member listing calls it "Asset Recharge Center" (https://www.mhi.org/members/115328, read as a search excerpt only, not fetched). The kiosk label in the owner's photo prints a web domain, which is not reproduced here because the label also carries contact details (publication boundary); the vendor's public site is cited below. It is a self-service device-custody locker for shared work devices: a touchscreen kiosk with "expandable modular locker banks and a cloud-based management platform", programmed "to release the mobile device with the most charge, alert managers when a device has not been returned, and allow employees to flag damaged devices" (https://experiencearc.com/introducing-arc-chargeitspots-new-mobile-device-management-locker-3/). That page also says ARC "contains an audit trail for device check-ins, effectively preventing employees from checking out a second device before having returned the first one", and that broken devices are kept out of circulation "unless it's been cleared by a supervising manager". The About page (https://experiencearc.com/about/) says it "Works with all major brands like Zebra, Honeywell, Apple, and Verifone", "allows for over-the-air software updates to devices", "Integrates with company logins, employee badges, and mobile device management tools" and "Connects to business systems like payroll, ticketing, and task tracking". It is sold into retail, grocery, warehouse, parcel, airline, manufacturing and healthcare.

Integration surface: the vendor says it integrates, but I found nothing public. Two web searches turned up no API, webhook, SDK or developer documentation for ChargeItSpot ARC. The hits named "Arc" (arc.gbci.org, CData Arc, Arc XP) are unrelated products. Every integration fact here is a vendor marketing claim, and none of it has been tested. The site's shrink, time and overstock percentages are vendor-stated without a method and are not reproduced in this proposal.

What the photo shows: one ARC kiosk with "Pick Up Device" and "Return Device" buttons. The serial number, support phone and support email on its label stay out of the tree (publication boundary).

proposals.ownerRequirementRead:
The owner's words, recorded verbatim as his direction: "...using the puck which is replacing of your ID badge/key card/2fa/MFA all of the above this device is the token for that user and cannot be duplicated and or replicated its hard locked once it's enrolled and registered to that person only way it's cleared is by factory wipe only super admin of the system can do without additional verification and validation making it impossible to break and or hack."

Translated into requirements the repo can hold truthfully:

(R1) One token that replaces badge, keycard, 2FA and MFA becomes: the puck MAY serve as the single carried credential. It may cover the door applet, the IdP passkey and the session attach, and already does in C2 and A4 (SESSION_PUCK :429ff, :554). CONFLICT for the owner: docs/PURPOSE.md:38 (canonical, DR-020) says 'The factor is the customer's choice, and the grid is agnostic to it.' The requirements text can make the puck one offered factor, not the required one. Making it mandatory is a PURPOSE change only the owner can make.

(R2) 'Cannot be duplicated or replicated' becomes: a non-exportable private key generated inside a secure element. Registration is accepted only with attestation and an authenticator-model allowlist enforced by the IdP (SESSION_PUCK :162, :257). Replacement always uses a NEW keypair, never a copy (:212). This is a proven, testable property, not 'clone-proof'.

(R3) 'Hard locked once enrolled to that person' becomes: the binding is the IdP registration mapping employee to credential ID to authenticator model/serial to issuance and revocation state (:216-224). Puck 9 (BUILD_BACKLOG.md:1044) and assigned mode (:551ff) add a tighten-only check that the puck presented matches the subject and device. Per DR-043 item 2 the lock lives in the IdP, not in a SignalGrid key database.

(R4) 'Cleared only by factory wipe' becomes a hardware fact the owner needs to know. FIDO CTAP 2.1 §6.6 authenticatorReset (https://fidoalliance.org/specs/fido-v2.1-ps-20210615/fido-client-to-authenticator-protocol-v2.1-ps-errata-20220621.html) needs only 'evidence of user interaction' and, on a key with no display, a request 'within 10 seconds of powering up'. It 'Invalidates all generated credentials' and disables enterprise attestation. So anyone holding an off-the-shelf key can wipe it, and 'only the super admin can clear it' cannot be a hardware property. The wipe does make the puck inert, which is the fail-closed outcome. The protected step is RE-BINDING: a new IdP registration for a person. That is where the super-admin control belongs.

(R5) 'Only super admin, with or without additional verification'. The sentence parses two ways: (a) only a super admin can wipe or re-bind, and only after additional verification; (b) a super admin can do it without additional verification and everyone else needs it. Both readings are recorded next to the quote. The proposal, not a decision: re-binding and revocation run through the IdP/PACS admin under the existing two-person pattern (lib/dual-control types.ts:88; DUAL_CONTROL.md:15, 'a single compromised or coerced credential should not be enough'). That suits either reading and removes a single-admin point of compromise. CONFLICT for the owner: if 'super admin of the system' means a SignalGrid super-admin who holds keys or enrolment, that contradicts DR-043 item 2 (no SignalGrid key database) and SESSION_PUCK :353 (no parallel identity administration). That would be a doctrine change, not a requirement.

(R6) 'Impossible to break or hack' becomes: the repo states proven properties (non-exportable key, attestation enforced, reissue with a new keypair, revocation sequence), points to the threat table (:205-212), and keeps the fail-closed rule. A puck that is absent, unknown or reported only by a mechanical sensor never loosens the answer: unknown attach is at least step_up (attach.ts header, DR-043 item 3a), and a mechanical-only attach counts as unknown (SESSION_PUCK new-rows table). 'Impossible' stays the owner's word, never the repo's (DR-043 item 5; SESSION_PUCK :400).
proposals.landingPlace:
The landing place is a dated section in docs/SESSION_PUCK_HARDWARE_HYPOTHESIS.md, 'Credential binding and reset (owner note 2026-10-02, DR-055 amendment)', plus an in-place amendment to DR-055 in docs/DECISION_RECORDS.md (owner-reserved to merge, writable on a PR). The ARC kiosk lands as a single cross-reference line in that section plus a RESOURCE_INTAKE row. It does not get a new matrix row.

Why this place: DR-055 is the existing refinement record. It 'amends nothing in DR-043's text; it adds to it' (DECISION_RECORDS.md:3505), and it was already amended in place for the 2026-09-24 owner note, so the 2026-10-02 note follows the same precedent. The hypothesis page already holds the C1-C7 and assigned-mode sections in the same shape.

Why not the alternatives:
- Amending DR-043 directly would break the pattern of leaving DR-043's text untouched and stacking refinements in DR-055.
- A new HARDWARE_PARTNER_MATRIX or SIGNAL_SOURCE_CATALOG row for ARC is wrong because matrix :17 already names ARC and :40-95 already maps its claims. A second row would duplicate it.
- A kiosk connector directory is wrong because the event contract and custody-ledger already model pickup and return vendor-neutrally, and no public ARC API exists to adapt to.
proposals.gapClosed:
The puck page has a lifecycle (SESSION_PUCK :216-224) and a lost-credential sequence (:212), but nothing on who may reset or re-bind a puck. It also lacks the hardware fact that a CTAP reset is available to whoever holds the key, and it has no answer to the owner's 'hard locked / super-admin factory wipe' requirement. A grep of the puck page and docs/ for 'super admin', 'factory wipe/reset' and 'authenticatorReset' found nothing about the puck. The only hits were unrelated Knox, DDM-re-enroll and resolution text.

A second gap sits next to it: no gate catches absolute-security wording. scripts/check-launch-claims.mjs OVERCLAIM_MARKERS (:426-430) contains only the three 'evaluated today' regexes. No script under scripts/ matches 'unhackable', 'clone-proof', 'hack-proof' or 'tamper-proof'. 'puck' is not in DEFERRED_NOUNS (:471-472). So buyer copy saying 'the unhackable puck replaces your badge' would pass every gate today. The ban exists only as prose, in DR-043 item 5 and SESSION_PUCK :400.
proposals.claimDiscipline:
Owner's words (recorded verbatim as direction, never as a repo claim): 'cannot be duplicated and or replicated', 'hard locked', 'only way it's cleared is by factory wipe only super admin', 'impossible to break and or hack', 'replacing your ID badge/key card/2fa/MFA all of the above'.

Sentences the docs MAY carry (all marked design target, deferred, not shipped):
- 'The puck is designed around a non-exportable key generated in a secure element; the IdP accepts its registration only with attestation from an allowlisted authenticator model.'
- 'Replacement always issues a new keypair; no key is copied.'
- 'The binding to one person is the IdP registration, revoked through the IdP and the PACS.'
- 'A factory reset (CTAP authenticatorReset) erases the puck's credentials and leaves it unusable; binding it to anyone again requires a new IdP registration, proposed to require two authorized administrators.'
- 'An absent, unknown or mechanically-reported puck never loosens a decision.'
- 'ARC-class dispensing kiosks are a candidate read-only custody signal source; the kiosk stays the system of record.'

Sentences the docs may NOT carry, in any tense:
- unhackable, impossible to hack or break, clone-proof, cannot be duplicated, tamper-proof
- only the super admin can wipe it (false for the hardware, per CTAP §6.6)
- the puck replaces the customer's badge or MFA (conflicts with PURPOSE.md:38)
- any ARC integration, partnership or certification
- ARC's 93%/84%/75% or shrink figures as fact

Which gate catches an over-claim: today, none mechanically. The computed task says scripts/check-launch-claims.mjs denies 'impossible to hack', 'cannot be duplicated' and 'unhackable'. That is false: its OVERCLAIM_MARKERS (:426-430) hold only three 'evaluated today' regexes, no script under scripts/ matches those words, and 'puck' is not in DEFERRED_NOUNS (:471-472). The ban exists only as prose in DR-043 item 5 and SESSION_PUCK :400. Task ARC-2 is the fix.

Gates that do apply today:
- check-launch-claims rule 3 catches unhedged 'custody' or 'badge binding' in buyer copy.
- check-known-false-claims catches only claims already registered in docs/agent/FALSE_CLAIMS.json.
- check-cited-paths catches bad path:line citations.

votes.reason: Direction is right: it makes a CTAP reset leave the puck inert, which fails closed. But R5 says re-bind and revoke run 'under the existing two-person pattern', and that pattern has no such class. lib/dual-control/src/types.ts:33 and :88 list only break_glass, privileged_config, bulk_data and unknown. The section must also say an absent or unreadable IdP binding means unbound, never already enrolled. This is the iOS managedBool lesson (CLAUDE.md, no policy default from the absence of managed configuration). Amended change: add to the ARC-1 section a fail-closed clause that a puck with no IdP binding, a wiped puck, or an unreadable binding state is unknown, so step_up at minimum and never allow, and state that re-bind needs a new elevated-action class (currently unmodelled) plus two authorizers, naming a single super-admin credential as the failure to avoid.

Checked in the tree. scripts/check-launch-claims.mjs:426-430 holds only the three evaluated-today regexes. DEFERRED_NOUNS at :471-472 has no puck. A grep of scripts/*.mjs and scripts/src for unhackable, clone-proof, impossible to hack and cannot be duplicated returned no hits. The ban exists as prose only, so the gate is a real gap.
